query_text: Long payloads produce a token that begins with a dot; I do not understand how the library decides to shrink it and how it restores the original on the way back.

query_text: After we replaced our application's secret with a new one, links that were mailed out before the change all stopped working at once.

query_text: After we replaced our application's secret with a new one, links that were mailed out before the change all stopped working at once.
justification: signer.py normalises a single key or an iterable of keys into the secret_keys list used for rotation.

query_text: I plugged in a custom encoder that produces raw bytes and now reading values back gives errors about decoding, although writing worked fine.

justification: timed.py (impl): raises BadTimeSignature('timestamp missing') when the unsigned result has no separator, i.e. the token was not produced by a timestamp signer.

query_text: URLSafeTimedSerializer.loads(token, max_age=60) fails with a 'timestamp missing' error for a token that was created by URLSafeSerializer.dumps.
justification: timed.py sets TimestampSigner as the signer class, which is why the timed serializer expects a timestamp in the token.

query_text: serializer.loads_unsafe(token) returns (False, None) for a string without any dot, even though I expected to see the payload.

query_text: serializer.loads_unsafe(token) returns (False, None) for a string without any dot, even though I expected to see the payload.
justification: signer.py raises BadSignature without payload when the separator is absent, which is what makes payload None.

query_text: We want SHA-256 instead of the default hash for every signature our serializers create; where is the default digest chosen and how can it be overridden per serializer?

query_text: Two services sign the same data with the same secret but different default salts so they reject each other's tokens; which defaults apply to salt and separator?
justification: serializer.py defaults salt to b'itsdangerous' for the serializer (a different default than the signer).

query_text: During a migration tokens signed with an older hash algorithm must still verify; how are fallback signers configured?
justification: serializer.py class-level default list of fallback signer parameters (empty since 2.0).

query_text: During a migration tokens signed with an older hash algorithm must still verify; how are fallback signers configured?
justification: serializer.py: yields the main signer, then builds a signer for each fallback entry (dict, tuple or class).

query_text: Tokens created with a custom salt cannot be loaded back with the default one although the secret key is identical; trace how the salt reaches the signing key.
justification: serializer.py: picks the salt (argument or self.salt) and passes it to the signer class.

query_text: Tokens created with a custom salt cannot be loaded back with the default one although the secret key is identical; trace how the salt reaches the signing key.
justification: serializer.py: the loads path builds signers with the salt given to loads, default self.salt.

query_text: Tokens created with a custom salt cannot be loaded back with the default one although the secret key is identical; trace how the salt reaches the signing key.
justification: signer.py mixes the salt into the derived key (concat / django-concat / hmac), so different salts give different keys.

query_text: A token whose time stamp part is damaged raises Malformed timestamp; where is the time stamp encoded into the token and decoded again?
justification: timed.py: decodes ts_bytes with base64_decode and bytes_to_int and raises BadTimeSignature('Malformed timestamp').

query_text: A token whose time stamp part is damaged raises Malformed timestamp; where is the time stamp encoded into the token and decoded again?
justification: encoding.py turns the packed 8-byte big-endian value back into an int.

query_text: A token whose time stamp part is damaged raises Malformed timestamp; where is the time stamp encoded into the token and decoded again?
justification: encoding.py packs the timestamp int into bytes with leading zero bytes stripped; used by TimestampSigner.sign.

query_text: InvalidSchema: No connection adapters were found for 'ftp://example.com/file'

query_text: CookieConflictError: There are multiple cookies with name 'sessionid'
justification: cookies.py raises CookieConflictError with exactly this message when more than one cookie matches name/domain/path.

query_text: requests.exceptions.MissingSchema: Invalid URL 'example.com/api': No scheme supplied. Perhaps you meant https://example.com/api?
justification: models.py raises MissingSchema with this message when parse_url returns no scheme.

query_text: A file upload that was partly read is not sent again from the beginning after the server answers with a redirect, so the second request goes out with a truncated body or the library gives up saying it cannot replay the body.
justification: utils.py seeks the body back to the recorded _body_position and raises UnrewindableBodyError when it cannot.

query_text: A file upload that was partly read is not sent again from the beginning after the server answers with a redirect, so the second request goes out with a truncated body or the library gives up saying it cannot replay the body.
justification: sessions.py: decides `rewindable` from _body_position and Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding and calls rewind_body before re-sending on each hop.

query_text: Sending an empty POST without any payload makes some servers answer 411 length required because no length header is present on the outgoing message.
justification: models.py sets Content-Length to 0 for methods other than GET/HEAD when there is no body; this is the logic that governs the header.

query_text: My script logs in to a website and gets bounced to a different website; afterwards my login details show up in that other website's access logs.

query_text: My script logs in to a website and gets bounced to a different website; afterwards my login details show up in that other website's access logs.
justification: sessions.py: deletes the Authorization header on redirect when should_strip_auth says so, then re-applies netrc credentials.

query_text: The text of the web page comes out with garbled accented letters when the server does not say which character set it uses.
justification: models.py: decodes content using self.encoding, falling back to apparent_encoding, with errors='replace'; wrong guess yields mojibake.

query_text: The text of the web page comes out with garbled accented letters when the server does not say which character set it uses.
justification: utils.py returns ISO-8859-1 for text/* without a charset, which is the usual source of garbled UTF-8 pages.

query_text: session.get() to the intranet address 10.0.0.5 goes through the corporate proxy although my no_proxy variable lists 10.0.0.0/8.
justification: utils.py evaluates no_proxy (host suffix, IP and CIDR forms) and decides whether to skip proxies; reached from Session.send via resolve_proxies.

query_text: session.get() to the intranet address 10.0.0.5 goes through the corporate proxy although my no_proxy variable lists 10.0.0.0/8.
justification: utils.py is the CIDR membership test that should_bypass_proxies uses for IPv4 hosts when no_proxy contains a network.

query_text: requests.post(url, json={'score': float('nan')}) fails with an error about out of range float values not being JSON compliant.

query_text: session.get(url, headers={'X-Token': 'abc\n'}) raises InvalidHeader about return characters in the header value.
justification: utils.py raises InvalidHeader 'Invalid leading whitespace, reserved character(s), or return character(s) in header value' when the validator regex does not match.

query_text: session.get(url, headers={'X-Token': 'abc\n'}) raises InvalidHeader about return characters in the header value.
justification: utils.py is the entry that validates name and value; called from PreparedRequest.prepare_headers.

query_text: I set session.verify = False but HTTPS calls still fail certificate verification as soon as REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is set in the environment.

query_text: I set session.verify = False but HTTPS calls still fail certificate verification as soon as REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is set in the environment.
justification: sessions.py decides which of request vs session setting is used; for non-dict values the request-level setting (here the env bundle) is returned.

query_text: How is the maximum number of redirects configured? I raised the limit but the exception about too many redirects still appears at thirty.
justification: sessions.py: raises TooManyRedirects when len(resp.history) >= self.max_redirects.

justification: adapters.py builds the urllib3 PoolManager from num_pools/maxsize/block.

query_text: Proxy credentials embedded in the proxy address (http://user:pass@proxy:3128) are not applied correctly: the Proxy-Authorization header is missing for plain HTTP targets after a redirect.

query_text: Proxy credentials embedded in the proxy address (http://user:pass@proxy:3128) are not applied correctly: the Proxy-Authorization header is missing for plain HTTP targets after a redirect.
justification: utils.py extracts username/password from the proxy URL used by both of the above.

query_text: Cookies that a server sets on a redirect response are not sent on the next hop of the redirect chain.

query_text: Cookies that a server sets on a redirect response are not sent on the next hop of the redirect chain.
justification: cookies.py merges the session jar into the request jar for the redirected request.
